text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The number of deputies in the conservative True Path Party coalition partner who want to go into alliance with the main opposition Motherland Party is growing.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan scraps plans to spend $107 billion on mega projects and channels the funds into small-scale projects that would grab votes.
MILLIYET
- Secularist army wants elections to be held under an independent government.
- Another election would raise the inflation rate and damage the Turkish lira.
HURRIYET
- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal says he may form an alliance with the rival Democratic Left Party in possible early elections.
- The monthly inflation rate is expected to be six percent for May.
YENI YUZYIL
- True Path leader Tansu Ciller tried to placate dissidents in the party by guaranteeing they will not be dropped as candidates in early elections.
- A declaration of democracy will be read in factories by workers and employees on Friday in order to protest at the Islamist-led government.
RADIKAL
- Erbakan's Islamists defend fellow Welfare MP Sevki Yilmaz, criticised for his fiery speeches.
DUNYA
- Wheat production increased in the western Aegean region.
- Turkey's fish sector demands low interest rate credits to compete internationally.
ZAMAN
- Court releases two policemen charged in security scandal.
CUMHURIYET
- Teachers' union to protest at state neglect of education.
